claim: The EBS direct APIs can create EBS snapshots, write data directly to snapshots, read data on snapshots, and identify the differences between two snapshots.
question: What can the EBS direct APIs do?

values.display: write data directly to your snapshots
read data on your snapshots
identify the differences or changes between two snapshots

evidence.quote: You can use the Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) direct APIs to create EBS snapshots, write data directly to your snapshots, read data on your snapshots, and identify the differences or changes between two snapshots.

claim: With the EBS direct APIs you can create incremental snapshots directly from on-premises data, for quick disaster recovery.
question: How can on-premises data become an EBS snapshot for disaster recovery?

values.display: incremental snapshots directly from data on-premises

evidence.quote: You can create incremental snapshots directly from data on-premises into EBS volumes and the cloud to use for quick disaster recovery.

claim: The GetSnapshotBlock and PutSnapshotBlock APIs support a 512KiB block size.
question: What block size do the EBS direct APIs GetSnapshotBlock and PutSnapshotBlock use?

values.display: 512KiB

evidence.quote: GetSnapshotBlock and PutSnapshotBlock APIs support 512KiB block size.

claim: EBS snapshots cannot be accessed with the regular Amazon S3 API; they are only available through the Amazon EC2 API.
question: Can you read EBS snapshots with the Amazon S3 API?

values.display: only available through the Amazon EC2 API

evidence.quote: No, snapshots are only available through the Amazon EC2 API.

note: The EBS direct APIs (ebs-faq-direct-apis-capabilities) also read snapshot data; the FAQ answer contrasts with the S3 API only.

claim: You do not need to unmount a volume to take a snapshot: snapshots can be taken in real time while the volume is attached and in use.
question: Do volumes need to be unmounted to take a snapshot?

values.display: while the volume is attached and in use

evidence.quote: No, snapshots can be done in real time while the volume is attached and in use.

claim: Snapshots only capture data that has been written to the EBS volume, which might exclude data cached locally by the application or OS.
question: What data can a snapshot of an in-use volume miss?

values.display: only capture data that has been written
locally cached by your application or OS

evidence.quote: However, snapshots only capture data that has been written to your Amazon EBS volume, which might exclude any data that has been locally cached by your application or OS.

claim: For consistent snapshots of a volume attached to an instance, AWS recommends detaching the volume cleanly, taking the snapshot, and then reattaching the volume; for root volumes, it recommends shutting down the machine.
question: How do you get a consistent snapshot of an attached data volume and of a root volume?

values.display: detaching the volume cleanly
shutting down the machine

qualifiers.scope: EBS volumes attached to an instance

evidence.quote: To ensure consistent snapshots on volumes attached to an instance, we recommend detaching the volume cleanly, issuing the snapshot command, and then reattaching the volume.
For Amazon EBS volumes that serve as root devices, we recommend shutting down the machine to take a clean snapshot.

claim: By design, a snapshot of an entire 16 TB volume should take no longer than a snapshot of an entire 1 TB volume; actual time depends on factors such as the amount of data changed since the last snapshot.
question: Does a snapshot of a 16 TB volume take longer than one of a 1 TB volume?

values.display: no longer than the time
16 TB volume
the amount of data that has changed

evidence.quote: By design, an EBS Snapshot of an entire 16 TB volume should take no longer than the time it takes to snapshot an entire 1 TB volume.
However, the actual time taken to create a snapshot depends on several factors including the amount of data that has changed since the last snapshot of the EBS volume.

claim: Each snapshot has a unique identifier, and you can create volumes from any of your existing snapshots, which allows point-in-time recovery.
question: Are EBS snapshots versioned, and can you restore from an older one?

values.display: a unique identifier
based on any of their existing snapshots

evidence.quote: Each snapshot is given a unique identifier, and customers can create volumes based on any of their existing snapshots.

note: The FAQ does not use the word 'versioned'; 'point-in-time recovery' comes from the FAQ question text.

claim: You can restrict public access to snapshots in an account by enabling Block Public Access for EBS Snapshots.
question: How do you stop EBS snapshots in an account from being shared publicly?

values.display: Block Public Access for EBS Snapshots

evidence.quote: You can also restrict public access to snapshots in an account by enabling Block Public Access for EBS Snapshots.

claim: Enable Fast Snapshot Restore when you are concerned about data-access latency when restoring a snapshot to a volume and want to avoid the initial performance hit during initialization; use cases include VDI, backup and restore, test/dev volume copies and booting from custom AMIs.
question: When would you use Fast Snapshot Restore?

values.display: avoid the initial performance hit during initialization
booting from custom AMIs

evidence.quote: You should enable FSR on snapshots if you are concerned about latency of data access when you restore data from a snapshot to a volume and want to avoid the initial performance hit during initialization.
FSR is intended to help with use cases such as virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI), backup & restore, test/dev volume copies, and booting from custom AMIs.

claim: Enabling Fast Snapshot Restore does not speed up snapshot creation; it improves restoring data from the snapshot to volumes.
question: Does enabling FSR make snapshot creation faster?

values.display: do not speed up snapshot creation time

evidence.quote: FSR-enabled snapshots improve restoring backup data from your snapshot to your volumes. FSR-enabled snapshots do not speed up snapshot creation time.

claim: FSR is enabled on a snapshot in the Availability Zone where the initialized volumes will be restored, and each AZ where it is enabled gets its own credit bucket.
question: At what scope is Fast Snapshot Restore enabled?

values.display: enable-fast-snapshot-restores
its own credit bucket

evidence.quote: To use the feature, invoke the new enable-fast-snapshot-restores API on a snapshot within the availability zone (AZ) where initialized volumes are to be restored.
Lastly, each AZ in which the snapshot is FSR-enabled gets its own credit bucket independent of other AZs.

claim: One FAQ answer says FSR can be enabled or disabled on account-owned snapshots only and cannot be applied to shared snapshots.
question: Can FSR be applied to shared snapshots, according to the FAQ answer on enabling FSR?

values.display: FSR cannot be applied to shared snapshots

qualifiers.scope: FAQ answer 'How do I enable Fast Snapshot Restore (FSR)?'

evidence.quote: FSR can be enabled or disabled on account-owned snapshots only. FSR cannot be applied to shared snapshots.

note: Contradicts ebs-faq-fsr-shared-snapshots-allowed in the same FAQ page (a later answer says FSR can be enabled on shared snapshots). Behavior lens should settle it from the user guide (ebs-fast-snapshot-restore).

claim: Another FAQ answer says you can enable FSR for public snapshots and for all private snapshots shared with your account, and only your account is billed for that FSR.
question: Can you enable FSR on a public or private snapshot shared with you, and who pays?

values.display: all private snapshots shared with your account
only your account will be billed

evidence.quote: Yes, you can enable FSR for public snapshots as well as all private snapshots shared with your account.
Note that only your account will be billed for the FSR of the shared snapshot.

note: Contradicts ebs-faq-fsr-own-snapshots-only in the same FAQ page.

claim: When the FSR credit bucket is full, up to 10 initialized volumes can be created from an FSR-enabled snapshot at once; volume creations beyond the limit proceed as if FSR were not enabled.
question: How many fully initialized volumes can you create at once from an FSR-enabled snapshot, and what happens beyond that?

values.display: up to 10 initialized volumes
as if FSR is not enabled

qualifiers.scope: per FSR-enabled snapshot, per Availability Zone

evidence.quote: When filled, up to 10 initialized volumes can be created from an FSR-enabled snapshot at once.
Volume creations beyond the limit will proceed as if FSR is not enabled on the snapshot.

claim: To estimate the FSR credit bucket size and fill rate, divide 1,024 by the snapshot size; a 100 GiB snapshot has a maximum balance of 10 credits and refills 10 credits every hour.
question: How is the FSR credit bucket size estimated?

values.display: divide 1,024 by your snapshot size
10 credits every hour

qualifiers.scope: per FSR-enabled snapshot, per Availability Zone

evidence.quote: To estimate your credit bucket size and fill rate, divide 1,024 by your snapshot size. For example, a 100 GiB FSR-enabled snapshot will have the maximum balance of 10 credits with a fill rate of 10 credits every hour.

claim: When you delete a snapshot, its FSR is automatically disabled and FSR billing for it ends.
question: What happens to Fast Snapshot Restore when you delete the snapshot?

values.display: automatically disabled

evidence.quote: When you delete a snapshot, the FSR for your snapshot is automatically disabled and FSR billing for the snapshot will be terminated.

claim: Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager and AWS Systems Manager can coordinate freeze, flush I/O and unfreeze of an application or database together with the start of EBS snapshots, to automate application-consistent snapshots.
question: How do you automate application-consistent EBS snapshots?

values.display: Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager and AWS Systems Manager
freeze, flush I/O, and unfreeze

evidence.quote: You can use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager and AWS Systems Manager (SSM) to coordinate freeze, flush I/O, and unfreeze of your application or database as well as the initialization of EBS Snapshots.
